findings.passage: Confidence is medium. Type 3 is the closest rival; Type 6 is live.
findings.problem: The article states Type 7 at medium confidence, but its own argument and the evidence record say no discriminator separates Seven from Three: 'A choice would settle it... None is on record,' her 2025 criteria 'move toward Three,' what leans Seven is 'small and specific,' and the Carrie episode, the on-set split and the staged essay all fit Three equally. Six is also left live. After the jury's fixes the Three case (working since ten, producer at 15 and 18, 'I'm still going to win,' constant outreach, 'work begets work,' shame vocabulary, status as protection) is at least as well evidenced as the Seven case, which rests on stated preferences from promotional Q&As and on how she tells stories on a comedy podcast. The standard calls for a sourced discriminator the strongest alternative fails, and for a research hold when none exists. She does not qualify as an open case: she has worked publicly since 2012 and has a deep first-person record. This cannot be repaired by rewording.
findings.acceptance_test: Research adds at least one sourced, dated item that Type 3 does not explain as well as Type 7, or the reverse: a recorded choice where advancement and enjoyment pulled apart, or a named director, showrunner or producer describing in their own words how she works and what she tracks. The type answer, FAQs and title then state a confidence the body's argument supports. If the new evidence favors Three, the run is refreshed with the expanded jury.

findings.passage: "I wasn't willing to do the show had I not been given a producer role," she told the Television Academy's emmy magazine. "So to pull me away from my education, which is really important to me, it had to be something that was worth it."
findings.problem: The two quoted sentences are separated in the source by her stated reason for the condition, which the article drops: 'The only way for me to tell the most accurate story possible and to do it right was to have more involvement in the show creatively.' She gives the same reason in three other opened sources: Variety ('she also wanted to make sure the show got it right'), The Hollywood Reporter ('The character needed to be authentically represented, and in order for that to be true, I would have to serve a bigger role') and Wonderland. The section then says 'the credit was not the point' without saying what she says the point was, meets it with 'A person who cared a great deal would say the same thing,' and the Type 3 section and FAQ list the condition as ambition evidence. A central anecdote is told without the subject's own explanation, and the missing half is the half that does not favor the Type 3 reading.
findings.acceptance_test: The 'One condition' section states her given reason in her attributed words from the Television Academy piece or The Hollywood Reporter, at the point where the condition is told. The skeptical sentence may stay. Where the Type 3 section or the FAQ uses the condition, nothing implies it was unexplained. C12's passage and note are updated to match.

findings.passage: Two weeks later, at the end of another episode, the hosts held a mock trial, with the show's producer as bailiff, on whether music should always be on. She ruled for music.
findings.problem: The trial was not about whether music should always be on. Crooked's episode page and transcript call the segment 'The Ickuation Room' and the topic 'Hookup Playlists... Ick or Yum,' and the two co-hosts argue for and against music during sex. She rules 'Yum wins, music should be playing when I'm doing nothing and when I'm doing it all.' The article's paraphrase misstates what the linked source shows, in the scene the profile closes on and under two quotations the type hypothesis counts (C54, C55). An accurate description also serves the argument better: she turned a debate about hookup playlists into a statement about never sitting in silence.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence names the actual topic in plain words (a mock trial on hookup playlists, or on whether music should play during sex) and gives her ruling in or close to her words. C92's claim and passage are corrected. The quotations and the last three sentences are unchanged.

findings.passage: Two weeks later, at the end of another episode,
findings.problem: The time reference has no anchor. The sentence opens a new section directly after 'That is the record as of November 10, 2026,' and the episode it counts from (August 11, 2022) was last mentioned five sections earlier. A reader cannot tell what it is two weeks after until the citation at the end of the paragraph.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence dates itself, for example by naming August 2022 or 'two weeks after that first episode.'

findings.passage: the story became the first thing her new audience heard, as comedy.
findings.problem: The transcript opens with a cold-open riff about the show being 'birthed,' then theme music; the prednisone line and the clinic story come after. It was the first story she told, not the first thing the audience heard.
findings.acceptance_test: The wording matches the transcript, for example 'the first story her new audience heard.' 'She opens the first episode wired' is adjusted or left only if it is clear the line follows the theme music.

findings.passage: So the restraint is narrow, and circumstance accounts for most of it: a host guarding her parents' house, a child actor told a drink could end her career.
findings.problem: In the sentence after the hook quotation she gives a third reason: 'I didn't want to drink when I was younger because I always felt so outside of my body and I felt like drinking would take me so much further.' The edit removed it. She also answers the question the paragraph leaves open, saying the conversation with her mother 'propelled me into just not being like the biggest drinker, even as someone who is currently 21.' Listing two reasons and handing the remainder to Type 6 slightly overstates what is unexplained.
findings.acceptance_test: One clause notes that she gave a further reason that falls under the limit stated in the type section and is not counted, without the author interpreting it; or the paragraph reports her own statement that her mother's warning is why she is still not a big drinker. The Type 6 pointer is scaled to match.

findings.passage: Thornton is the only witness to the improvising, in [two interviews]
findings.problem: Thornton says it in at least three: Digital Trends' Carrie cast interview also has her telling Totah 'you are such an amazing improviser.' The limit the sentence states still holds (one witness, with Totah present), but the count is wrong.
findings.acceptance_test: The count is corrected or made open ('in junket interviews'), and the Digital Trends interview is added to the evidence record with C62 updated.

findings.passage: She kept writing on a job where no credit asked her to.
findings.problem: In the same Nylon answer she says the production had asked her view in the first week of pre-production ('they were like, What do you think?... From then on, it was an open conversation') and that Jakeways replied 'Can you just send it to me?' Without that, 'no credit asked her to' and 'got her way' make an invited contribution read as an uninvited one.

findings.passage: "And the process is so fun. I love auditioning," the ten-year-old told her hometown paper. "You have to accept when you don't get it, that something else will come up," she said of rejection.
findings.problem: The two quotations are printed in the reverse of their order in the Davis Enterprise, where 'And the process is so fun' follows the rejection sentence. Each is verbatim, but the leading 'And' now continues from nothing.
findings.acceptance_test: The quotations appear in source order, or the first begins at 'the process is so fun' without the 'And.'

findings.passage: > "I love learning. I love being in class. But I also think as actors we have a mandate to kind of live our lives to the fullest extent."
findings.problem: Her next sentences tie the reason to her work: 'I just pull from my life... In order to have stuff to pull from, I have to make memories,' and Cero frames college as important 'for herself and her work.' The edit cut that continuation. The FAQ then offers the mandate line on the Seven side of the ledger. A reason given in service of the craft is one a Three would give too, and the reader should see that.
findings.acceptance_test: The body or the FAQ says in a clause that she tied living fully to having material for acting, so the reason is not presented as pure appetite. The same check is applied to 'tells her hard stories as comedy' in the 60-word answer and type FAQ, which should carry the body's scope (on her comedy podcast) or not claim more than three instances from 2022 and 2023 support.
